claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have a son, Alex, who's 18 and still living at home with me. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand his current situation.

Since Alex is 18, the key question is: Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's still in sixth form doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. A-levels at sixth form would generally count as approved education.

Just to confirm a few more details:

1. Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. A few more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Does Alex work, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work. He's focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions:

1. Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or would this be a new claim?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This would be a new claim. I haven't claimed Child Benefit for him before.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. One final question to complete my assessment:

Is there anyone else who is claiming or could claim Child Benefit for Alex (for example, another parent or guardian)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's no one else claiming for him. It's just me who's responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 18 years old and still in approved education (A-levels at sixth form)
- Under UK Child Benefit rules, you can continue to claim for a child under 20 if they remain in approved education or training
- Alex doesn't work 24 hours or more per week, which means he hasn't triggered any disqualification rules
- You live in the UK, you're responsible for Alex, and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You can go ahead and make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. 

**Important note:** Please be aware that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit Tax Charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might need to pay some or all of it back through your tax return.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
